## BGLRS Chapter 4 Problem 1

The evaluation of the labour supply response to a tax cut can be quite different in a dynamic setting from what it is in a static setting. Discuss the relative impact of a permanent versus transitory tax cut on labour supply, and compare the analysis to the static model.

## BGLRS Chapter 4 Problem 2

Consider the two-period dynamic labour supply model discussed in this chapter. What, if anything, happens to current labour supply if the interest rate rises from 2 percent to 10 percent?

## BGLRS Chapter 4 Problem 4

Use your knowledge of household production theory to indicate the following

a\) The expected effect of a wage increase on the wife's labour supply

## BGLRS Chapter 4 Problem 4

b\) The expected effect on the demand for children of an increase in the wage of a wife

## BGLRS Chapter 4 Problem 4

c\) Why the substitution effect for labour supply may be larger for women than men

## BGLRS Chapter 4 Problem 4

d\) The effect on one spouse's labour supply of his or her spouse's disability where the spouse requires home care

## BGLRS Chapter 4 Problem 4

e\) The effect on this same spouse's labour supply if the government provided financial compensation to the family
